title: Held, Not Touched
logline: A gem-cutter in Ratnapura brings a rough stone close under a single lamp and looks at it for longer than seems reasonable, ignoring everything else in the room until its faults and its worth both become visible.
human_question: What changes when attention stops scattering and holds one thing for a long time?

premise.story: A day, or several, in a small gem-cutting workshop, following one stone from rough form to finished cut, through the cutter's held, undistracted looking.
premise.place: A gem-cutting workshop in a gem-trading town.
premise.experience: Close, patient, almost uncomfortable attention on one small object, and the value that only shows up after a long look.

concept_links.why: The source's own image for deep concentration is someone who wants to truly know an object: bringing it close, shutting out the room, and looking long at its colour and marks until it is completely clear [C013-P:L48–L52]. The film keeps this as a working image, not a claim about the cutter's inner state.
As attention holds in this way, some things that felt necessary fall away one by one; the film can show a narrowing of movement and talk without naming it as doctrine.

A skilled cutter can pick up a stone, settle into the work, stop exactly when needed and look back over what was done, the ordinary craft version of a mastery the source describes for meditative absorption [C099-P:L69–L79].

what_camera_could_observe: The rough stone under different light, turned slowly
The cutter's stillness, breathing, the room otherwise ignored
Small adjustments, rejected angles, the first facet catching light
The finished stone weighed, valued, sold or kept
what_must_be_real: The cutter's actual trade, risk and skill. The film must not claim the cutter is meditating or has any inner attainment.

possible_arc.opening: A rough stone arrives; the cutter turns it under a lamp.
possible_arc.turn: A difficult decision about where to cut, made only after long looking.
possible_arc.ending_open: The stone leaves the workshop, for a buyer or a client. Reality decides the ending.

requirements: A working gem-cutter willing to be filmed over a real commission
Good light control for close macro photography
Time to follow one stone through several sessions

suggestions.name: Ratnapura
suggestions.why: Sri Lanka's best-known gem-trading and cutting town.
suggestions.access_notes: Many small workshops; a specific willing cutter must be found.
suggestions.verify: Access to a specific workshop and cutter is unverified.

risks: Overclaiming a spiritual state for ordinary skilled work
Trade secrecy around value and sourcing
Becoming a craft showcase with no stake
drop_if: No cutter will allow a real commission to be filmed start to finish

connections.note: Both are close studies of craft attention narrowing and refining, one on a single stone, one across a graduated set of vessels.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
